source_text: Σοφία δὲ ἐν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐξεταζομένη, καὶ διὰ προσώπου φαίνεται φωτίζουσα τὸν κεκτημένον· ὥσπερ οὖν ἀναίδεια, μίσους εὐθὺς ὀφθέντα ἄξιον ἐκεῖνον ἐλέγχει, ᾧπερ ἐνῴκησε. Πάνυ δὲ χρὴ ἐπιμελῶς τοῖς τοῦ βασιλέως προσέχειν λόγοις, ὅρκον δὲ ἐκ παντὸς τρόπου φεύγειν, μάλιστα τὸν εἰς Θεοῦ ὄνομα γινόμενον. Ἐφίστασθαι δὲ ὅμως προσήκει λόγῳ πονηρῷ· ἀλλὰ φυλάσσεσθαι ἅπασαν τὴν εἰς τὸν Δεσπότην βλασφημίαν. Οὐ γὰρ δὴ ἐπάγοντός τι μέμφεσθαι ὑπάρξει, οὐδὲ ἀντιλέγειν τοῖς τοῦ μόνου δυνάστου καὶ βασιλέως δόγμασι. Βέλτιον δὲ, καὶ λυσιτελέστερον ἐμμένοντα ταῖς ἱεραῖς ἐντολαῖς, λόγων τῶν πονηρῶν ἐκτὸς καθεστάναι. Σοφὸς γὰρ ἀνὴρ ἐπίσταται καὶ προγινώσκει τὴν εἰς καιρὸν κρίσιν, ὅτι δικαία ἔσται. Πάντα γὰρ τὰ ἐν τῷ βίῳ τῶν ἀνθρώπων πράγματα περιμένει τὴν ἄνωθεν κόλασιν· πλὴν ὅ γε πονηρὸς, οὐ λίαν γινώσκειν ἔοικεν, ὅτι πολλῆς ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ οὔσης προνοίας, οὐδὲν ὁτιοῦν εἰς τὸ μετέπειτα λήσεται. Οὐ γὰρ οἶδε τὰ ἐπιόντα· οὐδὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν κατ᾽ ἀξίαν τις ἀναγγεῖλαι δυνήσεται· ὅτι οὐχ οὕτως τις ἰσχυρὸς ὑπάρξει, ὡς τὸν ἀφαιρούμενον τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ ἄγγελον κωλῦσαι δύνασθαι, οὐδέ τις ὅλως μέθοδος εὑρεθείη ἂν τοῦ παραγράφασθαί πως τὸν καιρὸν τῆς τελευτῆς· ἀλλ᾽ ὥσπερ ἐν πολέμῳ μέσῳ ληφθέντα, ἄφυκτα πανταχόθεν ἔστιν ὁρᾷν, ἀσέβεια δὲ πᾶσα ἀνθρώπου συνεξόλλυται.
thought_title: Wisdom and the Fear of God Under a King's Authority
orientation: The speaker continues Solomon's teaching, contrasting wisdom's radiance with shamelessness, urging careful attention to the king's words, avoidance of oaths (especially in God's name), resistance to evil speech, and guarding against blasphemy toward the Master, because divine judgment is certain and no one can escape death or oppose the sole Ruler.
pass_a_gloss: Wisdom, being examined in a human being, and through the face it appears enlightening the one possessing it. Just as shamelessness, hatreds being seen immediately, reproves that one as worthy in whom it dwelt. Very much it is necessary to pay careful attention to the words of the king, and an oath from every way to flee, especially the one coming into God's name. To stand against an evil word nevertheless is fitting; but to guard all blasphemy toward the Master. For not upon something coming upon one will there be occasion to find fault, nor to speak against the decrees of the only Potentate and King. Better and more profitable, abiding by the sacred commands, to be established outside evil words. For a wise man knows and foreknows the judgment in due time, that it will be just. For all things in the life of humans await the punishment from above; except the wicked one, not very much to know he seems, that much providence being upon him, nothing whatever into the afterward will he obtain. For he does not know the things coming upon him; for none of them will anyone be able to announce according to worth; because not thus anyone will be strong as to be able to hinder the angel taking away his soul, nor any method at all will be found to evade somehow the time of the end; but just as in the midst of war being caught, inescapable from everywhere it is to see, impiety and all of a human being is destroyed together.

lemmas.gloss: to pay attention to / attend to
to guard against / keep oneself from
is destroyed together / perishes along with

choices.english: Wisdom, being examined in a human being
choices.why: Literal rendering of the participle; 'examined' captures the testing/proving sense in context.
rejected: Wisdom when examined in a human

choices.english: through the face it appears enlightening
choices.why: Keeps the spatial 'through the face' and the active 'enlightening' rather than 'shining'.
Matches the glossary's sense of brazen impudence; contrasts with wisdom's radiance.
Plural 'hatreds' and passive 'being seen' kept literal; 'immediately' for εὐθὺς.
Adverb 'carefully' + 'attend to' is the standard literal sense; 'words' for λόγοις.
rejected: give careful heed to the sayings

choices.why: Strong verb 'flee' kept; 'avoid' weakens the urgency.

choices.english: the one coming into God's name
choices.why: Participle 'coming into' reflects the Greek construction; 'in God's name' would flatten it.
ἐφίστημι with dative = resist/oppose; 'stand against' preserves the posture.
Δυνάστης = Potentate/Ruler; 'only' modifies both titles; capitalised as a divine title.
rejected: the only mighty one and king

choices.why: Comparative of λυσιτελής; 'profitable' fits the wisdom literature idiom.
περιμένω = await/expect; 'from above' for ἄνωθεν keeps the spatial divine source.
rejected: wait for the punishment from on high

choices.english: evade somehow the time of the end
choices.why: παραγράφω metaphorically = cross out/evade; 'somehow' for πῶς keeps the indefiniteness.

bible_refs.note: Wisdom brightens the face: 'ἡ σοφία φωτίζει πρόσωπον'
Keep the king's command, avoid oaths, do not resist the king's word
Time and judgment, no one knows the future, no authority over the spirit/day of death
Fear God; the wicked will not prolong days

pass_b_english: Wisdom is examined in a human being, and it shows through the face and gives light to the one who possesses it. Shamelessness, on the other hand, immediately shows the person in whom it dwells to be worthy of hatred, as soon as it is seen. You must pay careful attention to the words of the King. Flee every kind of oath, especially one that comes into God's name. Still, you ought to stand against an evil word, but guard yourself from all blasphemy against the Lord. For when the only Potentate and King brings something upon you, there will be no ground for complaint, and no one can speak against his decrees. It is better and more profitable to abide by the sacred commands and stay clear of evil words. A wise man knows and foresees the judgment that comes at the proper time, because that judgment will be just. All the affairs of human life await punishment from above. Yet the wicked man does not seem to know this very well. Even though great providence watches over him, nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come. He does not know what is coming, for no one will be able to announce any of it as it deserves. No one will be strong enough to prevent the angel who takes away his soul, and no method whatever will be found to evade the time of the end. Like a man caught in the middle of battle, destruction is inescapable from every side, and all human impiety is destroyed together.

problems.quote: he will receive nothing at all for the future
problems.source_quote: οὐδὲν ὁτιοῦν εἰς τὸ μετέπειτα λήσεται
problems.why: λήσεται means 'will escape notice'. The source says nothing will be hidden hereafter. The English gives a different claim about receiving nothing.
problems.fix: nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come.

problems.quote: as soon as hatreds are seen
problems.source_quote: μίσους εὐθὺς ὀφθέντα ἄξιον ἐκεῖνον ἐλέγχει
problems.why: The source says shamelessness, once seen, exposes its owner as worthy of hatred. 'Hatreds are seen' loses 'worthy' and the object.
problems.fix: as soon as it is seen, shows that person to be worthy of hatred.

edits.old: He does not know what is coming, and no one will be able to report any of those things as they deserve.
edits.new: He does not know what is coming, and nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come.

edits.old: Shamelessness, on the other hand, immediately reproves the person in whom it dwells, as soon as hatreds are seen.
edits.new: Shamelessness, on the other hand, immediately shows the person in whom it dwells to be worthy of hatred, as soon as it is seen.

fixed: Replaced 'he will receive nothing at all for the future' with 'nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come' to correctly translate λήσεται (from λανθάνω, 'to escape notice') and the clause 'οὐδὲν ὁτιοῦν εἰς τὸ μετέπειτα λήσεται'.

Replaced 'as soon as hatreds are seen' with 'as soon as it is seen' and 'reproves the person in whom it dwells' with 'shows the person in whom it dwells to be worthy of hatred' to reflect 'μίσους εὐθὺς ὀφθέντα ἄξιον ἐκεῖνον ἐλέγχει' (when hatreds appear immediately, it reproves that one as worthy of them).

problems.quote: he will receive nothing at all for the future
problems.source_quote: οὐδὲν ὁτιοῦν εἰς τὸ μετέπειτα λήσεται
problems.why: λήσεται means 'will escape notice'. The sense is that, with providence watching him, nothing will be hidden from it. The English invents 'receive nothing' and loses the point.
problems.fix: Even though great providence watches over him, nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come.

problems.quote: He does not know what is coming, and nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come.
problems.source_quote: οὐδὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν κατ᾽ ἀξίαν τις ἀναγγεῖλαι δυνήσεται
problems.why: The claim that no one can declare any of the coming events adequately is missing. The English repeats the 'escape notice' idea instead.
problems.fix: He does not know what is coming, for no one will be able to announce any of it as it deserves.

problems.quote: it appears enlightening through the face of the one who possesses it
problems.source_quote: διὰ προσώπου φαίνεται φωτίζουσα τὸν κεκτημένον
problems.why: The possessor is the one wisdom enlightens. English makes his face the channel of the light instead.
problems.fix: It shows through the face and gives light to the one who possesses it.
problems.ruling: τὸν κεκτημένον is the accusative object of φωτίζουσα: wisdom enlightens its possessor. The English makes it 'face of the one who possesses it' and loses the object.

edits.old: Even though great providence watches over him, he will receive nothing at all for the future.
edits.new: Even though great providence watches over him, nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come.

edits.old: He does not know what is coming, and nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come.
edits.new: He does not know what is coming, for no one will be able to announce any of it as it deserves.

edits.old: and it appears enlightening through the face of the one who possesses it.
edits.new: and it shows through the face and gives light to the one who possesses it.

fixed: Fixed mistranslation of 'λήσεται' (source: οὐδὲν ὁτιοῦν εἰς τὸ μετέπειτα λήσεται): changed 'he will receive nothing at all for the future' to 'nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come' to reflect that providence leaves nothing hidden.
Fixed omission of 'οὐδὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν κατ᾽ ἀξίαν τις ἀναγγεῖλαι δυνήσεται': replaced the repeated 'escape notice' clause with 'for no one will be able to announce any of it as it deserves'.

Fixed agency in 'διὰ προσώπου φαίνεται φωτίζουσα τὸν κεκτημένον': changed 'it appears enlightening through the face of the one who possesses it' to 'it shows through the face and gives light to the one who possesses it' so that wisdom enlightens the possessor, not the face.

last_rejected.quote: Yet the wicked man does not seem to know this very well. Even though great providence watches over him, nothing at all will escape notice in the time to come.
last_rejected.source_quote: πλὴν ὅ γε πονηρὸς, οὐ λίαν γινώσκειν ἔοικεν, ὅτι πολλῆς ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ οὔσης προνοίας, οὐδὲν ὁτιοῦν εἰς τὸ μετέπειτα λήσεται.
last_rejected.why: The ὅτι clause is what he fails to know. English points “this” backward and states the providence claim on its own.
last_rejected.fix: Yet the wicked man hardly seems to know that, great providence being over him, nothing at all will pass unnoticed in the time to come.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'does not know this very well... Even though great providence watches over him, nothing will escape notice' keeps the ὅτι content in substance; 'this' is a loose but understandable rendering.
